name: Cytokines
summary: Who makes each cytokine and what it acts on, as one network. Macrophages make the inflammatory ones: IL-1 (fever), IL-6 (acute phase), TNF-α (endothelium, shock), IL-8 (neutrophils) and IL-12, which drives Th1 and NK cells; their IFN-γ activates macrophages in turn. Th1 and Th2 hold each other back (IFN-γ vs IL-4 and IL-10); Tregs damp Th1 with IL-10. Th2 cells make IL-4 and IL-13 (IgE), IL-5 (eosinophils, IgA). IL-2 grows T cells; IL-3 grows marrow stem cells. “Hot T-bone stEAK”: IL-1 hot, IL-2 T cells, IL-3 bone marrow, IL-4 IgE, IL-5 IgA, IL-6 aKute phase.
tissue: everywhere: made locally, many act at a distance

hypo.name: Hypothalamus
hypo.notes: Raises the temperature set point (fever) via prostaglandin E₂: IL-1, IL-6 and TNF-α are the endogenous pyrogens.

liver.name: Liver
liver.notes: Makes acute-phase proteins: CRP, fibrinogen, ferritin, hepcidin, serum amyloid A up; albumin and transferrin down.

endo.name: Endothelium
endo.notes: Activated: adhesion molecules (E-selectin, ICAM-1), leak, and in sepsis, shock.

mac.name: Macrophage
mac.notes: Makes the inflammatory cytokines (IL-1, IL-6, IL-8, IL-12, TNF-α); with dendritic cells, presents antigen and makes IL-12 to start Th1 responses. Activated in turn by IFN-γ.

neut.name: Neutrophils
neut.notes: Drawn in by IL-8 from macrophages and IL-17 from Th17 cells (also C5a, LTB₄, kallikrein, platelet-activating factor).

treg.name: Regulatory T cells
treg.notes: Make IL-10 and TGF-β, which damp Th1 cells and macrophages (peripheral tolerance). IL-6 holds them back (and with TGF-β tips naive T cells to Th17 instead).

th1.name: Th1 and NK cells
th1.notes: Both make IFN-γ, the macrophage activator; IL-12 drives them. Th1 cells also make IL-2.

tc.name: T cells
tc.notes: IL-2 makes T cells (helper, cytotoxic, regulatory) and NK cells grow; activated T cells make IL-3.

th17.name: Th17 cells
th17.notes: Make IL-17 (draws neutrophils), IL-21 and IL-22. Held back by IFN-γ and IL-4.

eos.name: Eosinophils
eos.notes: IL-5 makes them grow and activate (helminths, allergy, asthma).

th2.name: Th2 cells
th2.notes: Make IL-4, IL-5, IL-10 and IL-13: IgE, eosinophils, helminths, allergy.

bcell.name: B cells
bcell.notes: IL-4 and IL-13 switch them to IgE (and IL-4 to IgG); IL-5 to IgA.

bm.name: Bone marrow
bm.notes: IL-3 (like GM-CSF) makes stem and progenitor cells grow and differentiate.

il1.name: IL-1
il1.notes: Fever and acute inflammation; endothelial adhesion molecules; activates osteoclasts. Anakinra blocks its receptor. “Hot”: IL-1, fever.

il6.name: IL-6
il6.notes: Acute-phase proteins and fever. Tocilizumab blocks its receptor. “aKute”: IL-6.

tnf.name: TNF-α
tnf.notes: Endothelial activation and leak (septic shock), cachexia, fever; keeps granulomas intact. Infliximab, adalimumab and etanercept block it; screen for latent TB first.

il8.name: IL-8
il8.notes: The major neutrophil chemokine. “Clean up on aisle 8.”

il12.name: IL-12
il12.notes: Makes naive T cells Th1 and activates NK cells. IL-12 receptor deficiency: disseminated mycobacterial and Salmonella infections. Ustekinumab blocks IL-12 and IL-23.

ifng.name: IFN-γ
ifng.notes: Activates macrophages (killing, granulomas, more MHC), drives IgG switching, and holds back Th2 cells. The IFN-γ release assay tests for latent TB.

il10.name: IL-10
il10.notes: Anti-inflammatory: lowers MHC II and Th1 cytokines, inhibits activated macrophages and dendritic cells.

il4.name: IL-4
il4.notes: IgE and IgG switching, makes naive T cells Th2, holds back Th1. Dupilumab blocks its receptor. “stEak”: IL-4, IgE.

il13.name: IL-13
il13.notes: Like IL-4: IgE switching; mucus and airway hyperreactivity in asthma.

il5.name: IL-5
il5.notes: Eosinophil growth and activation; IgA switching. Mepolizumab blocks it. “steAk”: IL-5, IgA.

il2.name: IL-2
il2.notes: T cell and NK cell growth. Aldesleukin is recombinant IL-2; calcineurin inhibitors block its production; basiliximab blocks its receptor (CD25). “T”: IL-2.

il17.name: IL-17
il17.notes: From Th17 cells: draws neutrophils (and makes epithelium release chemokines); skin and mucosal defense against fungi and extracellular bacteria. Secukinumab and ixekizumab block it (psoriasis).

il3.name: IL-3
il3.notes: Bone marrow stem cell growth and differentiation. “Bone”: IL-3.
